title: Bulalo: Filipino Beef Shank and Marrow Bone Soup with Corn and Cabbage
summary: A slow-simmered Filipino beef soup: marrow-bone shanks cooked until falling apart in a clear, peppery broth, with corn on the cob, cabbage and bok choy.

ingredients.item: cross-cut beef shank with marrow bone (osso buco cut), 4-6 pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
corn cobs, each cut into 3 pieces
small green cabbage, cut into 4 wedges through the core
heads bok choy or pechay, halved
calamansi or lime, in wedges, to serve
fish sauce with chopped chilli, to dip

steps.title: Blanch the shanks
steps.text: Put the shanks in the stockpot, cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Boil hard for 10 min, then tip into the colander and rinse each piece under the tap to remove the grey scum. Wash the pot.

steps.title: Start the broth
steps.text: Return the shanks to the clean pot with the 3.5 litres water, the onion and peppercorns. Bring slowly to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Simmer slowly
steps.text: Keep the pot at a lazy simmer, partly covered, for 3-3½ h, skimming fat and foam often, until the meat is falling off the bone and the marrow is soft. Top up with hot water to keep the shanks covered.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Stir in the fish sauce and salt, then taste. The broth should be clean and beefy; add a little more salt only if needed.

steps.title: Cook the corn
steps.text: Add the corn and simmer 10 min.

steps.title: Add the greens
steps.text: Add the cabbage wedges and simmer 5 min, then the bok choy for 2 min, just until it wilts but is still bright.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Share the shanks, corn, cabbage and bok choy between deep bowls and ladle the broth over. Scoop the marrow out with a teaspoon, and serve with rice, calamansi and the chilli fish sauce on the side.

tips: Blanching and rinsing the shanks first is the secret to a clear broth.
Keep the pot at a lazy simmer; a rolling boil makes the broth cloudy and greasy.
Chill leftovers overnight and lift off the set fat for a cleaner broth.
A pressure cooker cuts the simmer to about 50 min at high pressure.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze the broth and meat (without the vegetables) for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
